## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Boys of Grand Pré School: Illustrated" by James De Mille (Gutenberg #56232; "B. O. W. C." series; Lee & Shepard, Boston)

### Main characters
- **Boys of the "B. O. W. C." (secret society):** Bart (leader, imaginative, improvises rhymes), Bruce Rawdon (brave but superstitious about ghosts; strong wrestler; leads Scott's Bay party), Arthur (Bruce's brother), Phil, Tom.
- **Other boys:** Jiggins, Bogud, Billymack, Johnny Blue, Sammy (Ram Ram), Muckle, David Digg, Pat (Irish, pranks, "Porky pine"/porcupine episode, owl/donkey prank). Harry Thompson (small boy frightened).
- **Solomon:** old African-American servant/cook, "Grand Panjandrum" of the B.O.W.C., dialect speech; calls himself "Gasperojum" jokingly; cook in "cool an airy 'partment"; flees money-dig in panic.
- **Captain Corbet:** venerable mariner, owns schooner *Antelope*; wife Mrs. Corbet; infant "babby"; uses a "mineral rod" (divining rod) bought from old Zeke, a "demon in human form". Snaps rod at end. Dialect speech.
- **Dr. Porter:** headmaster/doctor; Museum curator (archaeology); enthusiast of Acadians.
- **Mr. Long:** teacher; lawyer-like defender at trial; eloquent.
- **Mr. Simmons:** teacher (mineralogy).
- **Old Zeke:** poor witness; "rat" joke; sold the mineral rod.
- **Prosecutor** (unnamed farmer in trial): potato field, claimed $500 damage.
- **Pieter Schwab:** Dutch-accented justice of the peace ("Rhadamanthus").
- **Captain Pratt:** potato-freighter captain who raises the Antelope.
- **Mr. Smalley, Mr. Atkins, Bennie Grigg and Mrs. Bennie** (Scott's Bay hosts, lavish meal).
- **Mr. Slocum:** owner of escaped screech owl.
- **Gaspereaugians:** rival village boys of Gaspereau valley; big leader (unnamed, wrestled by Bruce, thrown into pool).

### Chapter-by-chapter events
**I.** Spring recess ends. B.O.W.C. at camp in woods (dam, pool). Solomon brings lunch, refuses to stay as Grand Panjandrum. Boys make bows, arrows, whistles. Captain Corbet appears ("Who goes there?" by Bart). Corbet shows a stick he calls a "mineral rod" that finds buried treasure. He pulls out junk (list of ~50 items) from hat, finds copper coin "LOUIS XIV. ROI DE FRANCE." Says his rod pointed at an old French cellar in the "Old French Orchard" behind Academy. Motive: money for his baby. Bart says the Acadians buried wealth (references Benedict Bellefontaine, wealthiest farmer of Grand Pré).

**II.** Description of Grand Pré scenery; Blomidon; Acadian history (expulsion, Evangeline reference, 2,000 taken from Grand Pré). Boys at cellar. Corbet's rod falls at middle of cellar. Boys plan midnight dig, magic rules (lights in multiples of 3 or 7, silence).

**III.** Midnight dig. Lights in pails/baskets; Bart lights them. Corbet nervous; Solomon terrified. Latin/English/Euclid "incantations"; hymn to "Rousseau's Dream" tune. Bruce digs with pickaxe, hits metal. Sudden roar. Panic; flight. Solomon runs to room, barricades door. Bruce goes back, others follow. They fill hole. Corbet cries, snaps rod, vows to quit digging.

**IV.** Sunrise description. Mr. Long asks boys to unload ballast and rebuild stone wall (reward: holidays). Antelope found capsized in Mud Creek, mast down. Corbet: "gone sucker"; sees it as "finger of Providence". Corbet served with writ by owner of wall (prosecution) — Mr. Long promises defense.

**V.** Night noises in attic (garret). Bart suspects Pat. Boys search attic; find nothing. Bart says he'll investigate.

**VI.** Trial in village hall before Justice Pieter Schwab. Prosecutor claims $500 damage. Witness Old Zeke ("rat" cross-examination). Mr. Long demolishes prosecutor (potatoes worth ~$40). Captain Corbet's baby defense. Case dismissed; prosecutor pays costs.

**VII.** Attic noises again; Bruce and Arthur check. Bart stays at home. Boys walk to Gaspereau valley; fish; ford through enemy territory unmolested. At camp they find Gaspereaugians there.

**VIII.** Bart and Solomon ambushed on path, captured, basket of provisions taken. Bart jokes, Solomon freed by Bart's loose hands. Bruce vs big Gaspereaugian: underhold wrestling, Bruce throws him into pool. Gaspereaugians withdraw ("Exeunt omnes Gaspereaugienses").

**IX.** Lunch at camp; roar heard again from direction of pasture. Boys investigate; Solomon follows. Discover a donkey (Dr. Porter's; bought from "ole scissa grinda") brays. Mystery solved. Solomon laughs hysterically.

**X.** Boys return to French orchard to dig for real with spades. Hit ironclad box; it turns out to be a rusty ploughshare. Also: colter, bolts, ox chain, iron pot, 13 copper coins ("UN SOU"), nails, spikes, horse/cow bone. Boys give them to Dr. Porter, who laughs.

**XI.** Doctor's Acadian history lecture. Boys present relics to doctor. Dr. Porter invites them to excursion to Blomidon (French fort).

**XII.** Excursion starts 4 a.m. Saturday; breakfast on North Mountain; Dr. Porter's long history of Acadians (1606 Port Royal, Utrecht 1713, neutrals, Braddock, expulsion 1755, schooners from Boston of Apthorp & Hancock).

**XIII.** Doctor leads party into woods (Barrens); lost. Reach cliff edge over Bay of Fundy.

**XIV.** Party divided: Bruce leads Scott's Bay group (Bart, Arthur, Tom, Phil, Pat); doctor leads Hall's Harbor group (Jiggins, Bogud, Sammy, Johnny, Billymack). Pat chases porcupine with pole; gets lost, reappears. Bruce's group also lost in circle.

**XV.** Reunion on the road: Pat returns; they find a road. They turn right.

**XVI.** Two groups meet in fog at ~8 p.m.; doctor realizes they're at Scott's Bay. Surf heard inland. Cottage of Bennie Grigg.

**XVII.** Bennie and Mrs. Bennie feed them (long menu). Sleep on haymow. Sunday services; doctor admits error. Monday walk back; return to Academy at 11, school delayed.

**XVIII.** Pat frightens small boys (Harry Thompson). Bart confronts; boys plan to expose Pat. Supper in Rawdons' rooms; Solomon's speech; bell tolls, knocks; Solomon flees.

**XIX.** Bruce discovers string from bell to Pat's room. Plan: donkey taken up to attic (carpet-wrapped feet, turnips). Donkey brays under Pat's room. Pat flees to Bart's room.

**XX.** Pat confesses. Owl (Mr. Slocum's screech owl) was the screech. Solomon scolds owl; Pat takes owl to Slocum. Mr. Long calls boys to his study; reprimands; relents after Pat and boys confess. Captain Corbet arrives with baby; Mr. Long leaves. Corbet's grievance. Relics given to Museum; Bart's poem "The True Theory of the Bone".

**XXI–XXII.** (Museum lecture; Louisbourg first siege 1745 with Pepperell and Vaughn; doctor's account.) Boys go to see Antelope; Captain Pratt is at wharf.

**XXIII.** Pratt salvages Antelope ("Hi ho, cheerly, men"); boys help. Boys send Pat to fetch Corbet.

**XXIV.** Pat left with baby (disastrous). Corbet's wife returns and rescues. Corbet shown Antelope; sails for Boston with potatoes. Waves and cheers; Antelope vanishes into fog bank.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Shadowed by a Detective; or, The Woman in Wax" by Virginia Champlin (Gutenberg #78812; orig. René de Pont-Jest, *La femme de cire*; Street & Smith, Magnet Detective Library No. 106, 1899; published as serial in Boston Globe 1884)

### Characters
- **Ada Ricard** (born Mrs. James Gobson; actually Kitty Bell, twin of Anna Bell): wealthy society woman; missing ear-cut under big diamond; missing right canine tooth (pearl lacking).
- **Willie (Honorable) Saunders:** stout cracker-merchant, Brooklyn manufacturer, Ada's lover; wears Highland costume at ball; grief-stricken.
- **Colonel Edward Forster:** Union officer, yacht *Gleam*, Captain Reynolds.
- **James Gobson:** Ada's brutal first husband (Buffalo); disappeared; tooth + ear cut on Ada (his doing).
- **Mary:** Ada's maid; took $100 bribe.
- **July:** former servant; recognized torn ear.
- **Robert Fowl:** former coachman; identifies body as Ada.
- **Thomas Cornhill:** Ada's earlier suitor, died.
- **Fat Kelly (chief of metropolitan police, New York):** rough, corpulent.
- **Captain Young ("Master Young"):** giant detective, brave but obstinate.
- **William Dow:** ex-Philadelphia physician turned detective; sometimes called Charles Murray (alias at Jamaica Plain); adopted ward Miss Jane (16); governess Mrs. Wandright.
- **Robertson Jr.** (of Robertson Brothers & Co., agency; elder Edward Robertson, rival of Kelly).
- **Coroner Davis** (Saint Vincent district); **Sheriff Mortimer.**
- **Dr. O'Neel:** Bellevue Hospital surgeon; autopsy report.
- **Albert Moor:** sculptor; made wax head/body cast.
- **Toby:** watchman on Wharf 43; his barrel of tar tied to corpse.
- **Thomas Bright and Davidson:** proprietors of Shakespeare's Tavern (Wharf 32, South St.).
- **Tom Katters:** driver; **Thompson:** livery stable keeper.
- **Macready:** Gobson's defense lawyer; **O'Brien:** State's lawyer; **Judge Douglas.**
- **Meyer:** hangman (broke leg); **Mr. Peters:** Tombs manager; **Rev. Mr. Midler:** Methodist chaplain.
- **Harris Burnett:** Gobson's new club friend, agent for Dow.
- **Charles Murray:** Dow's alias at Jamaica Plain.
- **John Butler:** trapper guide; **Jimin (Swift Deer):** Sioux chief; **Washah and Winka:** warriors; Winka's wife with gold bracelet; **Makeni:** bracelet recipient.
- **Captain Semmas:** commander Fort Dakota.
- **Jefferie Muller:** jeweler.

### Chronology
1. Winter 1865: Ada's masquerade ball at No. 17 East 23rd St. Three "Sioux" masks carry her off in landau. Coachman Tom Katters drives to Yorkville; masked man carries her by boat across East River to Greenpoint, where Colonel Forster's coupé waits; to Brooklyn; yacht *Gleam*.
2. Saunders at police (Fat Kelly) rebuffed; hires Robertson Jr. ($500 + $500). Robertson's report (Katters, steamer mate James Davis, Gleam at Staten Island).
3. Saunders and Robertson on steamer *Firefly* at night off Staten Island; collision in fog between Forster's yawl and Firefly's boat; cry heard; woman presumed drowned. Saunders gives sailors $100 each for silence.
4. Shakespeare's Tavern drunk sailors (Jim, Charley). Body found by Toby tied to tar barrel at Wharf 32 (Wharf 43 barrel). Taken to morgue at Bellevue.
5. Dr. O'Neel's autopsy: no drowning (no foam); suspected chloroform/ether; missing right canine; old scar lower left ear. Kelly sends Young.
6. Robert Fowl identifies as Ada; Saunders identifies and collapses confessing ("it was I who killed you"). Mary doesn't identify (later admits).
7. Albert Moor casts plaster; William Dow helps; the wax head displayed.
8. Coroner Davis; reward $100/$1000. Gobson suspected.
9. James Gobson walks in claiming insurance (Gresham Company $20,000); arrested by Young at morgue after pistol shot from Dow's ball disarms him.
10. Trial at Criminal Court: Gobson found guilty; sentenced to hang on 25th (Wednesday). Macready defends.
11. Day of execution: Meyer breaks leg; execution postponed. Gobson breakfasts with Rev. Midler. Ada arrives at the Tombs (alive; claims she was in Havana/at sea with Forster). Gobson released on $100 bail. Ada visits; Saunders confronts; Robertson's agent denied.
12. Trial revision: Forster testifies (name protected); Ada speaks; Gobson acquitted.
13. Dow goes to Omaha, Sioux country; purchases bracelet from Sioux via Winka's wife; Dow's proof that Gobson took Kitty Bell (not Ada) to Forster.
14. Ada (Mrs. Gobson, second marriage) living at Jamaica Plain, Boston; Barker's club; Gobson drunk. Ada begins affair with Charles Murray (Dow). Note: "Jane" spies on them.
15. Murray saves Gobson from robbery (staged by Harris Burnett's accomplices); Gobson brings Murray to villa.
16. Murray's letter to Captain Young to have warrant against Gobson from Davis. Dow's plan: Burnett delivers fake letter to Gobson with envelope "Mr. Davis, coroner". Gobson enters villa at night with dagger; stabs wax statue (Ada), not Kitty Bell. Shot fired by Gobson at the wax figure; Young and Dow arrest him.
17. Kitty Bell (Anna's twin; wife of Gobson first, took Ada's place) confesses; she and Anna baptized as twins at St. Joseph's, New Orleans. Anna murdered by Gobson; Kitty substituted; tooth broken by Gobson's tea/fainting; Mary's role.
18. Gobson returned to Blackwell's Island; leaps into river at planking, dragging guard; body found under Wharf 32 (same place as Ada's corpse). Kitty sentenced to a year; later released by Kelly, cafe success, then Paris. Saunders gives wax statue to Barnum's Museum eventually. Kelly re-elected with 20,000 more votes. Dow to take Miss Jane for trip; "terrible tie" hinted; event promised for later narration.

### Key quoted phrases
- Dow: "Who knows if this will not be more than a work of art, and if this woman of stone will not accuse herself some day."
- Gobson: "Now, Kitty Bell, you will not speak."
- Saunders: "Poor Ada! poor Ada!"
- Kelly: "Devil take William Dow."

(Note: the book also includes Street & Smith advertisements (Ripans Tabules, Buckingham's Dye, Magnet/Arrow library lists) which are not story content.)
